key_insight: SPG-Layout improves text-driven indoor scene synthesis by combining statistical object priors with a hierarchical, large-object-first layout strategy to better handle non-Manhattan spatial constraints.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical path toward generating more physically plausible 3D interior layouts for CAD, robotics, VR, and generative design workflows in irregular environments.
method: Uses statistical priors of object distributions to guide training and improve scene realism.
Adopts a hierarchical layout strategy that places large objects first to reduce geometric violations.
Targets non-orthogonal spatial relationships to balance semantic fidelity and physical plausibility.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on a new benchmark of 500 diverse non-Manhattan environments and report consistent gains over existing methods in both Manhattan and non-Manhattan settings.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the learned priors and the benchmark’s coverage of real-world non-Manhattan floorplans, so generalization to unseen architectural styles should be checked.
paper_title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments
